content:
This is the initial release of Hex, a computational algebra library for Lean that I started working on recently.

First, what is it not focusing on for now:

  • no symbolic algebra
  • no new tactics

Instead, it provides computational tools over concrete types. The initial release includes 6 packages

  • HexMatrix
  • HexRowReduce
  • HexDeterminant
  • HexBareiss
  • HexGramSchmidt
  • HexLLL

These packages have no dependencies (besides each other), but each one has a companion HexXYZMathlib repository that additionally depends on Mathlib and relates the concrete computations with the corresponding abstract theory in Mathlib.

I'll give more detailed descriptions of the contents of these libraries over in the #Computer algebra channel, but for now let me tease you with this graph:

This shows the performance of the LLL algorithm (lattice basis reduction) on an family of adversarial inputs, comparing

  • Lean and Isabelle native implementations (both fully verified algorithms; indeed the Lean implementation here closely follows the lessons learnt in the Isabelle development).
  • The unverified but highly optimized fplll library written in C.
  • Lean and Isabelle implementations which call out to fplll via an FFI shim, and then fully verify the result.

As you can see, the verified-in-Lean curves are quite good! The README and Manual include more detailed performance benchmarking.

(The default lll implementation is set up to automatically use the C backend if it has been imported, and gives slightly worse bounds on the length of the shortest vector, or one can use lllNative which uses the pure Lean implementation, and gives the expected bounds.)

For now there is more focus on the performance of compiled code than on kernel evaluation, but I'd like to improve both, and layer some calculational tactics on top.

These libraries (and more in the pipeline) are produced using spec driven development (i.e. a careful specification of the library written in natural language, followed by AI implementation, followed by human review and polish). Contributions to the libraries are welcome, and should start with a PR providing new specifications or updating existing specifications, before any code is written.

Future planned libraries include fast polynomial factorization over F_p and Int, efficient implementations of finite fields, real and complex root isolation, and efficient arithmetic with algebraic numbers. I'd love to collaborate on further additions.
Discussion thread at #Computer algebra > Discussion: Hex

I wrote a blog post about using Hex to perform the Coppersmith attack on RSA.

https://kim-em.github.io/blog/2026-7-7-lattice-basis-reduction-using-the-hex-lean-library/

It demonstrates using lattice basis reduction, and the integer polynomial factorization library that's in development. (And, of course, all written in Verso.)
